name: Stone Arch Road Bridge, Stewartstown Railroad
wikipediaTitle: Stone Arch Road Bridge, Stewartstown Railroad
facts: Stone Arch Road Bridge, Stewartstown Railroad, spans 27-foot-6-inch over Shrewsbury Township, built circa 1895 by the railroad itself, showcasing early steel girder design on stone abutments.
In 1995, the bridge earned a place on the National Register of Historic Places, cementing its status as a preserved relic of late‑nineteenth‑century rail infrastructure.

Though modest in size, the 8.38‑meter long Stone Arch Road Bridge exemplifies the Stewartstown Railroad’s efficient use of stone abutments to support lightweight girder spans during a period of rapid rail expansion.
